functional_invariants.formal_statement: All team members MUST be inside the green SAFETY AREA strictly behind the launcher (clear of the red forward and lateral DANGER ZONE / KEEP CLEAR area) before launching, and operators MUST wear gloves and goggles when servicing the aircraft or launcher.

source_ref.locator: Section 9 Safety area schematics, Section 1 warnings 3-4 p.3, and Quick checklist p.39

functional_invariants.formal_statement: Carriage MUST be secured by the safety lock pin (with carriage support levers in the upper position) before opening the main reservoir outlet valve (4), and the safety lock pin MUST be removed only immediately before launch. Pressing the launch trigger while the safety lock pin remains installed invalidates launch state and forces repeating all preparation steps.

source_ref.locator: Section 1 warnings 5 & 7, Section 3 Step 5 p.8, and Section 5 p.25-26

functional_invariants.formal_statement: Operators MUST NOT handle or disconnect any pneumatic tubing until verifying the main reservoir outlet valve (4) is closed; open valve (4) only immediately before launch and close it immediately after launch and between launches.

source_ref.locator: Section 1 warnings 6 & 8, Section 5 p.26, Section 6 p.27, and Quick checklist p.39

functional_invariants.formal_statement: Launch angle is fixed at 12 degrees (0.20944 rad), maximum payload mass is 30 kg, and maximum allowed launch velocity is 25 m/s. Operator MUST verify target pressure against Table 2 (5 to 14 bar internal compressor, 15 to 16 bar auxiliary) on the manometer (8) so 25 m/s is never exceeded.

source_ref.locator: Section 8 Technical Specifications, Table 2, and Section 5 p.24

functional_invariants.formal_statement: Forward support levers must engage forward aircraft slots first followed by rear levers into straight, parallel, tightly secured drone hardpoints with zero gap between lever lock pads and zero movement when the aircraft engine is throttled up and down; loose levers cause momentary piston over-acceleration that engages the internal pneumatic safety shutoff valve and causes launch failure.

source_ref.locator: Section 3 Steps 27-28 and Section 5 Step 10 p.24

functional_invariants.formal_statement: Pulling rope must be connected to the furthest reachable of 3 carriage slots, routed cleanly in the groove, tensioned via slots and regulating screw so it does not lean slack on the rail (which causes shock-load over-acceleration on launch) yet does not disengage the carriage rear locking mechanism, and replaced every 100 launches or immediately on wear, tear, or loose fibers.

source_ref.locator: Section 3 Steps 20-26 p.15-17 and Section 7.3 p.29

functional_invariants.formal_statement: Launched payload center of mass MUST lie inside the allowed 200 mm x 100 mm CG envelope above the carriage cradle, and the puller or pusher aircraft propeller MUST NOT enter the carriage exclusion region below the 155.5 mm (front) / 145 mm (rear) / 208.5 mm Propeller Safezone.

source_ref.locator: Section 10 PROPELLER SAFEZONE p.41 and ALLOWED CENTER OF MASS POSITION p.42

functional_invariants.formal_statement: All 4 carriage wheel bearings MUST be replaced every 100 launches (heating threaded area to ~250 deg C / 523.15 K and unscrewing left-hand shaft clockwise, then applying threadlocker and reinstalling counterclockwise), and the rail track groove must be lubricated with white lithium grease (WD-40 White Lithium Grease recommended).

source_ref.locator: Section 7.2 p.28 and Section 7.4 Wheel bearing replacement p.34-36

functional_invariants.formal_statement: Electronic controller enforces 14 bar maximum target pressure, 0.05 bar pressure hysteresis, and battery over-discharge protection turning the compressor OFF at <= 14.5 V (PWR LED blinking) with automatic restart after 5 s if battery voltage recovers > 16 V; replace battery with a fully charged 18V 6000 mAh cartridge after the 1st launch and at least every 2 consecutive launches.

source_ref.locator: Sections 4.2-4.4 p.22-23, Section 5 Step 13 p.26, and Section 7.1 p.28

functional_invariants.formal_statement: Trigger handle safety covers MUST remain closed at all times except launch execution; launch requires moving safety levers up, pressing both switches simultaneously for >= 2 s, and keeping trigger buttons pressed until the aircraft leaves the catapult so the main valve does not close prematurely.

source_ref.locator: Section 5 Step 12, Figure 5-3, and NB!/ATTENTION boxes p.25-26
